title: Revenue is not the same as cash
concept: Revenue is the value of sales earned during the period. Cash is the money currently available to pay bills.
formula: Revenue = units sold × selling price + other sales
skill: Read the top line before judging whether the company is healthy.

title: Cost of goods sold (COGS)
concept: COGS is the direct cost attached to the products or services sold this week. It rises when you sell more.
formula: Gross profit = Revenue − COGS / variable costs
skill: Separate direct unit costs from operating overhead.

title: Gross profit pays for the company
concept: Gross profit is what remains after direct costs. It must be large enough to pay salaries, rent, marketing, administration and financing costs.
formula: Gross profit = Revenue − Variable costs
skill: Judge whether the core product economics can support the rest of the business.

title: Gross margin makes businesses comparable
concept: Gross margin expresses gross profit as a percentage of revenue. A higher margin gives more room to pay operating expenses and survive shocks.
formula: Gross margin % = Gross profit ÷ Revenue × 100
skill: Track margin percentage, not only gross-profit dollars.

title: Fixed costs vs variable costs
concept: Variable costs move with sales volume. Fixed costs continue even when sales are weak, so a high fixed-cost base increases operating leverage.
formula: Total operating cost = Variable costs + Fixed/operating costs
skill: Know which costs disappear when volume falls and which do not.

title: Operating expenses (OpEx)
concept: Operating expenses are the costs of running the company beyond direct production: payroll, rent, marketing, administration, quality and similar items.
formula: Operating profit = Gross profit − Operating expenses
skill: Control overhead without starving growth or product quality.

title: Operating profit and EBITDA thinking
concept: Operating profit shows whether the business model works before financing and tax. This game currently uses an EBITDA-like operating measure because depreciation/amortization is not separately modeled.
formula: Operating profit ≈ Gross profit − operating expenses
skill: Separate operating performance from capital structure and tax.

title: Net profit: the bottom line
concept: Net profit is what remains after operating costs, interest, penalties and accrued tax. A company can grow revenue and still lose money.
formula: Net profit = Pre-tax profit − Tax accrued
skill: Always connect growth to profitability.

title: Profit is not cash flow
concept: Profit follows accounting recognition; cash tracks actual money movement. Inventory purchases, loan principal and tax payments can move cash differently from profit.
formula: Cash change = Ending cash − Previous ending cash
skill: Reconcile profit with cash before deciding how much the company can spend.

title: Break-even revenue
concept: Break-even is the revenue level where contribution from sales covers operating expenses. Below it, the company normally loses money.
formula: Break-even revenue = Operating expenses ÷ Contribution margin %
skill: Know the minimum sales level required to support the cost base.

title: Burn rate and runway
concept: When the company is losing money, runway estimates how long cash can support that loss rate before financing becomes necessary.
formula: Runway ≈ Cash ÷ Weekly burn
skill: React to shrinking runway before cash reaches zero.

title: Assets: resources the company controls
concept: Assets include cash, protected reserves, inventory and capitalized expansion assets in this simulation.
formula: Assets = Cash + Reserve + Inventory + Capitalized expansion assets
skill: Distinguish spending that disappears from spending that creates an asset.

title: Liabilities: claims against the company
concept: Liabilities are obligations the company owes, such as loans and tax payable. They reduce the owners' residual claim on assets.
formula: Liabilities = Debt + Tax payable + other obligations
skill: Measure obligations alongside assets, not in isolation.

title: The balance-sheet equation
concept: Book equity is the accounting residual belonging to owners after liabilities are deducted from assets. It is different from market valuation.
formula: Assets = Liabilities + Equity
skill: Use the balance sheet to understand financial structure.

title: Working capital and inventory
concept: Inventory can consume cash before it becomes an expense. Too little inventory loses sales; too much traps cash and may spoil or become obsolete.
formula: Cash tied in inventory = Inventory units × unit cost
skill: Manage liquidity as well as accounting profit.

title: Customer acquisition cost (CAC)
concept: CAC measures how much it costs to acquire a customer. Rising CAC can make growth destructive even when revenue increases.
formula: CAC = Acquisition spend ÷ customers acquired
skill: Compare acquisition cost with the value of the customer.

title: Lifetime value and LTV:CAC
concept: LTV estimates gross value from a customer over the relationship. Comparing LTV with CAC tests whether paid growth can create value.
formula: LTV:CAC = Estimated customer LTV ÷ Effective CAC
skill: Avoid scaling acquisition until customer economics are attractive.

title: Debt, interest and leverage
concept: Debt provides cash without ownership dilution, but creates interest expense and mandatory principal repayments that reduce financial flexibility.
formula: Debt-to-equity = Debt balance ÷ Book equity
skill: Compare the benefit of borrowed capital with the fixed cash burden it creates.

title: Tax accrual vs tax payment
concept: Tax expense may be recognized before the cash is actually paid. Tax payable accumulates as a liability until the payment date.
formula: Tax payable = Prior payable + tax accrued − tax paid
skill: Reserve cash for taxes even before the payment date.

title: Valuation is not the same as profit or book equity
concept: Valuation estimates what the company may be worth based on revenue, profit, customers and capital structure. It can move differently from cash or book equity.
formula: Game valuation = revenue value + profit value + customer value − debt + selected assets
skill: Understand the difference between operating performance, accounting equity and market value.
